lines.text: A fax arrives. Which patient's chart does it belong in?
lines.note: Illustrative incoming-document problem, no measured outcome.

lines.text: On September sixteenth, UT Health Houston reported its AI system handling that work.
lines.note: Report date, not launch date. UT Health is an orthographic separation of the same UTHealth Houston institutional name and the directed U-T pronunciation; no factual or spoken-word change.

lines.text: Staff used to read each fax and enter the patient details.
Now the software extracts those details and links the document to the chart.
It also sorts and separates documents, cutting down the filing work.
The university reports time saved. That is its own account.
lines.note: No magnitude or independent outcome certification.

lines.text: The report gives no appointment waiting times.
lines.note: Absence bounded to September university report.

lines.text: The clinic leaders can ask whether less filing means earlier care.
lines.note: Suggested evaluative question for the clinic leaders in the institutional setting, not a claim that they announced a study or that care improved. Added definite article does not change the source-backed scope.

lines.text: The fax reaches its chart. Earlier care is still a question.
lines.note: Editorial close: source-backed document linking resolves the opening. Earlier care remains an unanswered evaluation question because the report does not give appointment waiting times.
